name: Act of April 10, 1876 authorizing the sale of the Pawnee Reservation in Nebraska
nations: Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma (Chaui, Kitkehahki, Pitahawirata and Skidi bands)
promises: With the consent of the Pawnee expressed in open council, the Secretary of the Interior could appraise and sell the whole reservation set apart by the treaty of September 24, 1857, in 160 acre tracts, at no less than appraised value or $2.50 an acre.
The same Act provided a new reservation for the Pawnee in Indian Territory between the Cimarron and Arkansas rivers (Royce area 591).

breaches.what: The Court of Claims found that Congress, by an Act at 22 Stat. 68, 85, reserved from the sale this Act provided a 160-acre tract of the Pawnee reservation with its buildings, without the Pawnee's consent, and used it for a school for children of other tribes; no Pawnee was educated there after the 1876 removal.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Act of Congress, 22 Stat. 68, 85, as found by the Court of Claims, Pawnee Tribe of Indians v. United States, 56 Ct. Cl. 1 (decided December 6, 1920), Finding VI

source.title: Pawnee Tribe of Indians v. United States, 56 Ct. Cl. 1 (1920), Finding VI
source.publisher: Caselaw Access Project (Harvard Law School Library)

breaches.quote: The United States by act of Congress (22 Stat., 68, 85), without the consent of the Indians, reserved this 160-acre tract from sale.

today: In 1920 the Court of Claims found that a later Act of Congress took 160 acres of the reservation out of the sale without the Pawnee's consent; Congress later paid the appraised value of $960. The Indian Claims Commission's Pawnee case (Docket 10) describes the 1876 appraisal and the sales, which began July 15, 1878, but no finding that this sale broke a promise was found. The Commission did find the 1875 payment for a separate 4,800 acre strip (its Claim V) unconscionable; that is a different event. The Indian Territory reservation was ceded under the agreement of November 23, 1892.

nationVoice.summary: The Nation says that after years of trespass, theft, rape and murder by white settlers it sold its Nebraska reservation to the United States in 1874 and bought new lands from the Cherokee and Muscogee nations in what is now Oklahoma.

openQuestions: Whether the Pawnee consented in open council, and whether the sale proceeds were handled as the Act required, was not traced. The Commission noted that after the first auction sales continued without competition at the appraised price.
The Pawnee Nation's own history page (pawneenation.org) refused the request in this pass.
Area 590 is mapped to both this record and kappler-772 (the 1857 treaty).

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for "Pawnee" (opened 56 Ct. Cl. 1, 124 Ct. Cl. 324, 157 Ct. Cl. 134) and ICC "Pawnee Genoa school 160" (no decisions), "Pawnee 1876 appraised Nebraska reservation sale" (OSU 91, 404). Found: 56 Ct. Cl. 1 (1920), Finding VI, that an Act of Congress (22 Stat. 68, 85) reserved 160 acres from this sale without the Pawnee's consent; status raised from no-breach-found to broken. The case reported findings and conclusions on the tribe's claims; it made no money ruling on the 160 acres because Congress had already paid the appraised value.

The opinion prints the reimbursing Act as "approved March 3, 1883 (27 Stats., 612, 620)"; volume 27 of the Statutes at Large covers 1891 to 1893, so the year looks misprinted. The date of the Act at 22 Stat. 68 was not opened; neither date is used in the record.
compensation: The Court of Claims records that the 160 acres were appraised at $6 an acre and that Congress appropriated $960 to reimburse the tribe for that appraised value (27 Stat. 612, 620). How the rest of the sale proceeds were handled was not traced.

plain.promised: With the Pawnee's consent, the whole Nebraska reservation was to be appraised and sold, at no less than appraised value or $2.50 an acre, and the Pawnee moved to a new reservation in Indian Territory.
plain.happened: The Court of Claims found in 1920 that Congress later kept 160 acres out of the sale without the Pawnee's consent and used it for a school for other tribes.
plain.today: Congress later appropriated $960, the appraised value of the 160 acres. How the rest of the sale money was handled was not traced.
